text:
maria: Quick proposal drop — adding a per-service-account mapping table that binds API keys to (project_id, role_alias) pairs. Goal: enable fine-grained routing and RBAC without tearing down current long-lived key UX.
ashwin: interesting. is this trying to replace project-scoped keys or sit on top as a translation layer?
devin: I'd prefer a translation layer. migration path should be: existing key -> mapping entry + optional short-lived mint for cross-project.
maria: correct, translation layer first. runtime would check mapping table, then either allow direct evaluation or mint ephemeral creds for downstream project boundaries.
luis: two quick concerns: 1) telemetry/latency overhead on hot paths, 2) key churn explosion if we start minting widely.
maria: agreed. design tradeoffs I sketched:
- path A: keep key as-is for same-project calls (no extra hop).
- path B: for cross-project, runtime issues a short-lived ticket via internal minting service (100ms p50 target).
- path C: for trusted internal services we allow role_alias passthrough (no mint) but require allowlist + audit.
ashwin: how do we express role_alias in the SDK/requests? header? claim?
maria: prefer header now for minimal plumbing: `X-Redwood-Role-Alias: <alias>` with runtime validation. later expose in SDK as param so apps don't handroll headers.
devin: can we get away from header for server-to-server calls? headers are easy to forge if key leaks. maybe bind alias in mapping table and only allow header if mapping allows override.
maria: yes — mapping table has `allowed_overrides: []`. default is no override. header only honored if key.mapping.allowed_overrides includes alias.
luis: ok. telemetry: add metric `auth.mapping.lookup.latency` and `auth.mint.success_rate`. we should capacity test minting path under peak inference load (dedicated pools burst).
ops-bot: :rotating_light: reminder: any change touching minting path needs runbook update + canary gate in rollout pipeline.
ashwin: what's the authz evaluation order? evaluate project binding, then role_alias, then policy?
maria: evaluation order: 1) mapping lookup, 2) project affinity check, 3) if cross-project and no passthrough -> mint, 4) policy check against resolved principal. ensures least privilege and auditable mint events.
devin: migration: we should backfill mapping table from existing key metadata. add opt-in flag `enforce_mappings` per-org so customers can opt into strict checks.
luis: regression test ideas: 1) same-project p95 latency should be unchanged; 2) cross-project mint p50 under 200ms; 3) failure surface: fallback to legacy allow if mapping service unreachable for a short window (feature flagged).
maria: security notes: rotate default long-lived keys expiration to 6 months and encourage ephemeral by default for new keys. add telemetry spike alerts for `auth.mint.rate` to detect mass-service compromises.
ashwin: sounds good. can you post a short RFC doc (one-pager) with the schema for the mapping table + sample migration SQL and a short rollback plan?
maria: will do. dropping initial schema here for quick feedback:
```
-- service_account_mapping
service_key_id TEXT PRIMARY KEY,
project_id TEXT NOT NULL,
role_alias TEXT NOT NULL,
allowed_overrides TEXT[], -- list of aliases allowed via header override
enforce_from TIMESTAMP, -- when mapping starts being enforced
created_by TEXT,
last_seen TIMESTAMP
```

luis: looks fine. add `audit_log_id` or `last_mint_id` for quick correlation.
maria: good call — will add `last_mint_id`.
devin: thumbs up. low-risk incremental rollout plan: 1) read-only mapping table + metrics, 2) honor header for allowed overrides only, 3) enable minting behind feature flag, 4) org opt-in enforce.
maria: thanks — I'll post RFC + PR for the runtime check in ~24h. tagging @ashwin for infra sizing numbers for the minting service.
ashwin: noted. I'll run a quick capacity sketch and post numbers tomorrow.
ops-bot: :white_check_mark: RFC posted: link to doc (internal).
